items.title: Joe Williams interviewed by Leslie Gourse, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: I used to have some problems with Mr. Basie sometimes. I would ask, I’d say, “Hey, Bas’, I’d like to get an arrangement on” such and such a song. And he’d say, “Oh, you don’t need that thing. Sing the things you’ve been singing.”

ctx.x: No, no. You do what you do. I sing. And if I feel like I want to sing something I do it. I used to have some problems with Mr. Basie sometimes. I would ask, I’d say, “Hey, Bas’, I’d like to get an arrangement on” such and such a song. And he’d say, “Oh, you don’t need that thing. Sing the things you’ve been singing.” You know. If you let people, even those closest to you — and he was very close to me — if you let them discourage you from doing what you feel you want to do, in many instances it’ll leave you one…

say hey, you don’t need that. There’s no need for you do to that. You know like if you believe in it strongly, do it. And that’s what happened all the way along the line. I wanted to do a spiritual album since 1957. But the fellas didn’t want me to. People were enjoying some remuneration from my success as a quote unquote sox symbol — a sex symbol. A sox symbol you know. Yeah. As in a boxer, you know. They felt that if I were to do a spiritual album that it would take away from my aura as a sex symbol or…

items.title: 52157_Count Basie oral history interview
items.q: I worked with Joe Williams on and off

ctx.x: Then contradict me. I am saying it to you, not to anyone out there, right.

I will always say -- I always say that somebody is one of the best. I never say anybody who is the best of anything. I mean like -- I would say to me, who is the best piano, the best one, who is this guy saying who is the best. And just remember now how can I say that, and I worked with Ella, I worked with Billy Eckstine, I worked with Frank Sinatra, I worked with Joe Williams on and off, the
best, that's a hell of a thing for me to say with me when he's working with all these people and Sarah, and all these people. How can I say that.
